events.title: Traditional date of the death of Saint Patrick
events.description: By tradition Patrick, the Romano-British missionary to Ireland, died on 17 March, though the year is uncertain. His feast became Ireland's national day, celebrated by the Irish diaspora worldwide.
events.html: By tradition Patrick, the Romano-British missionary to Ireland, died on 17 March, though the year is uncertain. His feast became Ireland's national day, celebrated by the Irish diaspora worldwide.

events.title: British troops evacuate Boston
events.description: After Washington fortified Dorchester Heights with cannon hauled from Fort Ticonderoga, General Howe's army sailed for Halifax. The siege of Boston ended in an American success.

events.title: Stephen Perry patents the rubber band
events.description: Stephen Perry of the London firm Messrs Perry and Co patented bands made of vulcanised rubber for holding papers together. The humble invention became universal.

events.title: Einstein completes his paper on light quanta
events.description: Einstein finished a paper proposing that light comes in discrete packets of energy, explaining the photoelectric effect. It helped found quantum theory and earned him the Nobel Prize.
events.html: Einstein finished a paper proposing that light comes in discrete packets of energy, explaining the photoelectric effect. It helped found quantum theory and earned him the Nobel Prize.

events.title: Brussels Treaty creates a Western European defence pact
events.description: Britain, France, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg agreed to defend one another against attack. The pact paved the way for NATO in 1949 and later became the Western European Union.

events.title: US launches Vanguard 1 satellite
events.description: The grapefruit-sized satellite, mocked by Khrushchev, showed that the Earth is slightly pear-shaped. Long silent, it is the oldest human-made object still in orbit.
